sections.h2: When can I visit the Montmorency County register of deeds in Atlanta?
sections.html:
Deeds for the county go to 12265 M-32 West in Atlanta, mailing box 789, ZIP 49709. Phone 989-785-8079. The posted window is Monday through Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., and the county site adds that the counter stays staffed at midday.

The register is the constitutional recording officer for anything that transfers or burdens land here, including mineral interests along with surface interests. Each paper gets an exact receipt time, a liber and page, and a line in the entry book. Originals are scanned and sent to microfiche for off-site archive storage, and a tract index lets a searcher start from the legal description rather than a name.

The same staff chair the county plat board and take passport applications. Abstractors, title companies, mortgage lenders, oil and gas land agents and township assessors all rely on this counter, and the office describes itself as the starting point of the county's tax base.

sections.h2: What is Montmorency County like for a home seller?
sections.html:
Montmorency sits in Northern Michigan on the Lake Huron side, drained by the Thunder Bay River toward Alpena. The land area is 547 square miles, and most of it is state forest on the Grayling outwash plain, with jack pine barrens and lakes left by glaciers. The Legislature created the county in 1840 under an Ojibwe chief's name, renamed it in 1843 and organized it in 1881, and Hillman, the first seat, yielded to Atlanta in 1891.

Only 9,153 people lived here in 2020, which makes it the second-smallest Lower Peninsula county. The Census Bureau's estimate for July 2025 is 9,842, up 7.5%. A third of residents are 65 or older, and the average household has 1.92 people. The 2020 census counted 8,930 housing units with 51.6% of them vacant, a share that goes with a tourism economy of cabins, lake lots and trail traffic.

Atlanta itself is an unincorporated community of 720, 46 miles west of Alpena and 32 miles east of Gaylord. It calls itself the Elk Capital of Michigan and hosts a winter rally race. Hillman, a village of 605, lies 15 miles east-northeast, and Atlanta Community Schools serves the center of the county.

  • Median value of an owner-occupied home, 2020 to 2024: $158,600.
  • Median household income: $49,756.
  • Median gross rent: $686.
  • Mean travel time to work: 26.3 minutes.

Townships are Albert, Avery, Briley, Hillman, Loud, Montmorency, Rust and Vienna, plus the Village of Hillman.

sections.h2: How does recreation shape sales in Montmorency County?
sections.html:
Trail access drives much of the local market. The county's ORV, ATV and snowmobile trails are described as some of the best in the state, and it is one of the few counties that let ATVs ride public county roads, which links fuel stops, food and lodging in Hillman, Atlanta and Lewiston. Buyers who hunt, fish or ride often care more about where a parcel touches state forest or a lake than about square footage.

Farming is a smaller piece of the economy, built around dairy products and dry beans. Tourism services and retail form most of the base, so a house near the Thunder Bay River or a lake lot can read as a rental or a weekend place to a buyer. A seller should state the road type, the water frontage and any recorded easement in the listing, then confirm each against the register's index before the contract is signed.

sections.h2: Which forms and helpers does the Montmorency County register list?
sections.html:
The county page carries downloads for a quit claim deed, a warranty deed, an affidavit of affixture for a mobile home, a notice of intention to maintain mineral rights and a principal residence exemption form. It also posts fee sheets for statutory charges, copies and searches, commercial code filings, recording standards and transfer tax, with separate sheets for county exemptions, state exemptions and valuation.

For a cabin, hunting parcel or acreage, three items come up most.

  • A deed that repeats the legal description exactly, because the tract index runs on it.
  • A recorded survey when a boundary matters. The page lists several surveyors and independent searchers in the region.
  • Mobile home or mineral paperwork, when either appears in the chain of title.

Title companies in Atlanta, Alpena and Gaylord are also listed. One of them can draft the deed and order the search that a buyer will want, which the register's staff cannot do.

sections.h2: What does the Montmorency County register charge?
sections.html:
Michigan's judicature act sets $30.00 as the base recording charge, with $3.00 more for each extra instrument a single paper assigns or discharges. Searches by name run 50 cents a year with a $5.00 floor. A county that is not chartered cannot go above the state schedule, so the sheet on the county site is the number to follow.

Phone 989-785-8079 if you plan to mail a check and want the total confirmed.

sections.h2: How much transfer tax will a Montmorency County seller owe?
sections.html:
On a sale at the county median the combined bill lands near $1,367. The state takes $3.75 and the county $0.55 for every $500 of price or part of it, and the county treasurer receives payment within 15 days.

A deed for under $100, a land contract that keeps title with the seller until paid in full, and a corrective quitclaim all sit outside both taxes. For a parcel that crosses a county line, split the price and pay each county its share.

sections.h2: What happens to the tax bill after a cabin or house sells?
sections.html:
A sale resets taxable value. Under MCL 211.27a the next year's figure moves up to state equalized value, half of true cash value, and the buyer informs the local assessor within 45 days. A cabin held for decades can carry a taxable value far below that number, so the new owner may see a jump. A parent, child, sibling or grandchild who keeps a residence non-commercial is excepted, and so is a surviving spouse.

An inherited property counts as a transfer when it passes by will or intestacy to anyone outside those groups. Ask the township assessor which rule fits before you decide on a price. The Montmorency County treasurer can report the parcel's tax status before you set a closing date.

If the seller took the homestead exemption, it must be rescinded on Form 2602 within 90 days of the house ceasing to be the owner's home.

faqs.q: Is the Montmorency County register of deeds open at lunchtime?
faqs.a: Yes. The county site says the office stays open during lunch hours, with a weekday window of 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. The phone is 989-785-8079.

faqs.q: What is the combined transfer tax on a $158,600 house?
faqs.a: $1,367.40, split as $1,192.50 to the state and $174.90 to the county. The seller owes it, and the price is rounded up to the next $500 before the rates apply.

faqs.q: Can the office prepare my quit claim deed?
faqs.a: No. It records and indexes. The county page offers quit claim and warranty deed forms, but a title company or attorney should confirm which one fits your transfer.

faqs.q: How do I find out whether mineral rights were severed?
faqs.a: Ask a title company to search the chain of title. The register records mineral interests apart from surface interests, and the county page lists a notice form for keeping mineral rights.

faqs.q: Which county page lists Atlanta-area title companies?
faqs.a: The register of deeds page lists title companies in Atlanta, Alpena and Gaylord, as well as surveyors and independent searchers in the area.
